chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Khunays ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no determinism (jabr) and no relinquishment (tafwid), but rather a matter between the two matters. He said: I asked, 'What is the matter between the two matters?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'The example of that is like a man whom you saw committing a sin, so you forbade him, but he did not stop. Then you left him, and he committed that sin. It is not the case that because he did not accept your forbidding and you left him, that you are the one who commanded him to commit the sin.'

key_terms.أَمْرٌ بَيْنَ أَمْرَيْنِ: A matter between the two (the middle ground of free will within divine decree)
key_terms.تَفْوِيض: Relinquishment (God leaves humans entirely to their own devices)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia concept of 'Amr bayn al-amrayn' in contrast to Jabr and Tafwid?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the middle path of *Amr bayn al-amrayn*, rejecting the Mu'tazila's absolute relinquishment (*Tafwid*) and the Asha'ira's absolute determinism (*Jabr*). The analogy clarifies that while God commands and forbids, He does not coerce the will; thus, human agency is genuine, and divine responsibility is negated only when the individual freely ignores the warning, preserving both justice and free will within the Shia theological framework.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Kufi said, on the authority of Khunays ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn `Umar that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

“There is no determinism and thee is no relinquishment. Rather, the decree is between the two.” The reporter says: I asked, “What is the decree between the two?” He (AS) replied, “The example of that is of a man who was about to commit a sin. You saw him, and you told him not to do it. However, he did not stop. Then you left him, and he committed the sin. You abandoned him to his sin because he did not heed your warning. This does not mean that you encouraged him to sin.”
